transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I just can’t stop worrying. It feels like everything is hitting me at once—my marriage, whether I’m messing up at work, bills, stuff around the house I keep starting and not finishing. I keep thinking I’m failing as a husband and a father, and I don’t know how to turn it off.
Are there things you used to do or places you used to go that you're avoiding now because of your worries?

I’m not sure. I don’t think there’s a specific place I’m avoiding because of it. I mean, I still go to work and do the usual things. I just… I don’t know, I haven’t really noticed avoiding anything in particular.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I feel overwhelmed a lot, but I don’t know if I’d say I’m sad or down most of the time.
Are you avoiding any specific activities because of your worries?
I don’t think so. I can’t point to a specific activity I’m staying away from because of the worry. I still do the things I have to do—it just feels harder in my head.
Have you lost any weight recently?
I haven’t really noticed any weight loss recently. My weight seems about the same, as far as I can tell.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and you can't seem to get rid of?

Yeah. It’s mostly worries that just keep looping. Like even if I’m trying to focus on code at work, or if I’m working out and trying to breathe through it, one concern leads to another. I’ll start with something small, like a bad review, and then my mind jumps all the way to losing my job and my family being worse off because of me. I can’t seem to shut it off.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific rituals or behaviors to reduce your anxiety?
No, I don’t think so. I don’t have any specific ritual or thing I feel like I have to do to make the anxiety go away. I mostly just sit with it or try to keep going.
Have you experienced any episodes of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes and included symptoms like a racing heart or shortness of breath?

I’m not sure I’ve had something like that. I do get anxious, but I can’t really think of a clear episode where it suddenly peaked within a few minutes like that with a racing heart or shortness of breath.
Is your worry spread across many areas of your life or is it mainly focused on one or two things?

It’s spread across a lot of things. I came in because it feels like I can’t stop worrying about everything at once—my marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, house projects I keep not finishing, and just this feeling that I’m failing as a husband and father.
Do you find yourself avoiding social interactions because of your worries?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I avoid people in a clear way because of the worry. I might be quieter or less eager to make plans sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed myself avoiding social situations specifically.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

Yes. I feel wound tight almost all day, like I’m bracing for something. My shoulders are tense a lot, and I catch myself pacing between meetings or tapping things at chess club because sitting still feels really hard.
Do you feel like you've been distant or detached from your loved ones lately?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I feel detached exactly. Maybe distracted or not fully present sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed feeling distant from them in a clear way.
Have you been experiencing a lack of interest in activities you normally enjoy?

I don’t think so. I still do the things I normally enjoy, like going to chess club or relaxing with my usual hobbies. I might not feel as fully relaxed while doing them, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest.
Have you been having trouble sleeping because of your worries?

Yes. Most nights I’m exhausted, but once I’m in bed my mind just starts going—work stuff, money, things I said to my wife. I’ll finally fall asleep sometimes, but then I wake up around 3 or 4 and I’m already thinking through tomorrow’s problems, and I can’t get back to sleep.
Have your worries been interfering with your ability to function at work or at home?

Yes, definitely. At work it’s started to show up more. My manager has been noting things I missed in architectural details, which isn’t like me. And at home I’ll start projects and leave them half-finished, or I’m there physically but too distracted to really engage. That’s been leading to more arguments, and they keep getting worse.
Do you have thoughts that you consider irrational or unwanted, but that keep coming back to you?

Yes. I know they’re not always realistic, but they keep coming back. Like I’ll try to focus on the code in front of me, or try to breathe through a workout, and one worry just hooks into another. Pretty soon I’m imagining a bad review at work turning into losing my job, and then my family being worse off because of me. It’s hard to shut off once it starts.
Do you feel like you're able to experience a full range of emotions, or has your ability to feel emotions been affected lately?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think my emotions are gone or anything. I can still feel happy or frustrated or sad. Lately it’s more like worry is taking up so much space that it kind of crowds everything else out, but I wouldn’t say I can’t feel emotions.
Have you felt less emotional or less reactive to things that would normally upset or excite you?

I don’t think so, not really. I still get upset by things that would normally upset me, and I can still get excited sometimes. It’s more that I’m distracted or preoccupied a lot, so I may not show it the same way in the moment.
Do you often feel nervous or fearful for no apparent reason?

Yes. A lot of the time I feel nervous and I can’t point to one clear reason. It’s like everything piles up at once—my marriage, work, bills, things around the house I haven’t finished, and whether I’m letting my family down. I came in because I just can’t seem to stop worrying about all of it.
Have you been avoiding certain social or performance situations because you fear being judged or evaluated by others?

I don’t think that’s really the main issue for me. I’m not avoiding social or work situations because I’m afraid people will judge me. I might feel tense going into things, but it’s not specifically about being evaluated.
